title: ARQ_P01
description:
The project is based on the concept of the Impluvium, conceived as a spatial device for light, orientation, and connection to the landscape. The design responds directly to the site’s topography, with solar orientation and visual openness as key guiding principles.

The house is organized around two main volumes arranged in an L-shaped layout, creating a clear relationship between solid and void. Their intersection defines the core architectural gesture, allowing a functional separation between Day and Night areas while structuring the overall use of the house.

From this initial gesture, a continuous third volume completes the composition, forming a clear three-volume system. These volumetric intersections shape the building’s elevations and frame a central semi-cloister, where the swimming pool acts as the spatial and atmospheric focus.

The cloister is completed by a fourth, non-built element: an open void defined by the surrounding landscape, reinforcing the relationship between architecture, light, and place.
